solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hit and stumped round end of over

indicators.note: round says one word goes around another, here enclosing a single letter

parts.note: stumped means baffled, the same as stuck

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word over

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the batsman was hit and then stumped just as the over ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is a decoy: 'stumped' is just baffled, and 'end of over' is its last letter R, put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning delivered a blow, so it matches hit as a past verb.

clue.text: Recognise sailor hugging upper-class European

indicators.note: hugging says the sailor's word wraps closely around the letter for upper-class

parts.note: a salt is an old seafarer
U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A sailor embracing a posh European is acknowledging an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to acknowledge or honour them with a gesture, a synonym for recognise.

clue.text: Almost discover jerk's unsentimental

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to discover the truth is to realise it
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch; the 's is read as is and adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man who has nearly found out he is a jerk is still hard-headed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person sees things as they are, practical and without sentiment.

clue.text: Shout for joy, capturing Queen, guru's last piece

indicators.note: capturing says the cheering word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to cheer is to shout for joy
Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen, rather than the usual ER

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word guru's

explanation.surface: A chess player whoops on taking the queen with the master's final piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is Q here, not the more usual ER; the chess setting also hides that 'piece' is a draughts piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a counter used in the game of draughts or checkers, a playing piece.

clue.text: Fought advance with daughter embracing darling

indicators.note: embracing says the word for advance wraps around the endearment

parts.note: to come is to advance or approach
pet is an affectionate term like darling
D abbreviates daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone fought their way forward while their daughter hugged a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Competed means contended or vied against others, which is to have fought for something.

clue.text: Harbinger literary mariner raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo is the submarine commander in Jules Verne's novels

explanation.surface: A sea captain from a novel is held up as a sign of things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign foretelling the future, as a harbinger heralds what is coming.

clue.text: Shot phaser suppressing power, maybe

indicators.note: suppressing is read as holding something down within, so a letter sits inside
shot means wrecked or worn out, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A science-fiction ray gun is broken and its power cut, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and maybe are both adverbs expressing possibility without certainty.

clue.text: Aluminium sink set up for scientist

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the whole sequence is read upwards

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
the sun sets when it sinks below the horizon

explanation.surface: A metal sink has been installed for a researcher's laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the run AL+SET, read bottom to top. Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American electrical engineer and inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was a famous inventor and physicist who pioneered alternating current.

clue.text: Devotee getting record on impulse, oddly

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of impulse

explanation.surface: A fan bought a record on a whim, strangely enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or adherent of a teacher, which is a devotee.

clue.text: Was first to admit slob was idle

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: someone who led was in front, first in the race
an oaf is a clumsy lout or slob

explanation.surface: The front-runner let a slob in, and the slob did nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have loafed is to have lazed about doing nothing, which is being idle.

clue.text: Terribly serious following new obsession

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the abbreviation for new
terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a fresh fixation has become terribly grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis can be a compulsive fixation or anxiety, close to an obsession.

clue.text: Brief half of police catching a criminal

indicators.note: catching says those kept letters close around the rest
half of keeps three of the six letters of police, here the central three rather than a front or back half

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A short report says half the police force has caught a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of police' keeps the middle three letters LIC, not a front or back half; they wrap A CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, so it is terse or brief.

clue.text: Court's central point overturned in court case

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is simply court

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the word for a court case

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

indicators.note: overturned means the word for central point is turned backwards

parts.note: the nub is the crux or central point

explanation.surface: A judge's key ruling was overturned during the hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that hears and judges disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: One's back having taken in a distant expedition

indicators.note: having taken in says the reversed pair enclose the other letters
back means the letters for one's are read in reverse

parts.note: one's is short for one is, written I S
far means distant

explanation.surface: Someone back home has taken in a faraway place.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland trip, especially in Africa to see wildlife, a kind of expedition.

clue.text: A star rose rising up

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the colour word is read upwards

parts.note: rose is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A celebrity's rose climbs ever higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the past tense of rise but is the colour, a shade of RED, turned upwards. 'Up' is the sense in 'torn up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or into pieces, as in torn up or ripped apart.

clue.text: Cat litter's loose blends keeping hot

indicators.note: keeping says the jumbled letters hold another letter inside
blends means mixes up, so the letters of the fodder are combined in a new order

parts.note: here the s of litter's counts as a letter
H abbreviates hot on taps

explanation.surface: A cat's loose bedding mixes in with something warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' looks like part of the litter picture, but it is the definition; 'blends' rearranges LITTERSLOOSE around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black, orange and cream fur.

clue.text: Tireless Tsipras initially dividing Greece in broadcast

indicators.note: dividing says a letter splits the jumbled letters by going inside
broadcast means scattered widely, signalling the letters are spread and rearranged
initially picks the first letter of Tsipras

explanation.surface: A news report has the tireless prime minister splitting his country.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexis Tsipras was Prime Minister of Greece in 2015. 'broadcast' rearranges GREECEIN, and his first letter goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means full of vigour and stamina, so someone energetic is tireless.

clue.text: Yokels in endless quiet among pines

indicators.note: among says the shortened word sits inside the word for pines

parts.note: to pant for something is to yearn or pine for it

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ease is quiet or comfort

explanation.surface: Country folk live in endless calm among the pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pines' looks like trees but is a verb, long for: PANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are rural farm workers, often looked down on as yokels.

clue.text: Offensive former husband can be polite, possibly

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says their rude ex-husband can sometimes be courteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptionable means open to objection, liable to cause offence.

clue.text: Tease is acceptable in show

indicators.note: in places the word for acceptable inside the word for show

parts.note: to prove something is to show it is true
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Teasing is fine in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke someone is to goad or needle them, as a tease does.

clue.text: Outlaw gang pinches gear

indicators.note: pinches is taken as grips or squeezes, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A bandit gang steals equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or robber living outside the law.

clue.text: Wide bristles collecting rubbish

indicators.note: collecting says the two words gather the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A broad-bristled broom sweeps up litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, which is rubbish.

clue.text: Insect originally circling field

indicators.note: circling says the two clue words surround the answer within them

explanation.surface: An insect first flies in circles over a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' tempts a first-letter pick, but nothing is taken from the front: the answer runs across 'Insect originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a field or area of activity, such as the public sector.

clue.text: Freight vehicle on move

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A goods truck is on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by ship, plane or lorry, which is freight.

clue.text: Regimen broken eating acceptable dessert

indicators.note: eating says the jumbled letters take another letter inside them
broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: U means acceptable, as in socially U

explanation.surface: A dieter breaks their regime by eating a nice pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a sweet baked from whipped egg whites and sugar, served as a dessert.

clue.text: Pressure on unhealthy to get some medicine

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: ill means unwell or unhealthy

explanation.surface: A sick person is pushed to take their tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet, one dose of a drug, so a portion of medicine.

clue.text: Anaesthetic with nitrogen and oxygen kept in cold

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

indicators.note: kept in says one letter is held inside the word for cold

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A gas mix of nitrogen and oxygen is stored chilled for surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses and relieves pain, an anaesthetic agent.

clue.text: Hesitate, seeing female change

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Someone wavers when they see a woman change.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter is to lose confidence and waver, so to hesitate.

clue.text: Shifty about cooker left dirty

indicators.note: about says the word for shifty goes around the other letters

parts.note: sly means crafty or shifty
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A dodgy character around the stove left it filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy and careless in appearance, unkempt or dirty.

clue.text: Polishes, accepting corporal's first orders

indicators.note: accepting says the word for polishes takes a letter inside it

parts.note: to edit text is to polish or refine it

indicators.note: first picks the initial letter of corporal's

explanation.surface: A soldier shines boots after the corporal gives the first commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees or proclamations, which are orders.
